article_title: Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI
citation: Gyeong-Geon Lee and Xiaoming Zhai. (2024). Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07163
title: Visual Question Answering as a task at the intersection of computer vision, NLP, and knowledge representation
description: VQA is defined as a machine-learning task in which, "given an image and a natural language question about the image, the task is to provide an accurate natural language answer". The article frames VQA as lying in the intersection of computer vision, natural language processing, and knowledge representation and reasoning, requiring multimodal knowledge and evaluation for open-ended and multiple-choice questions. It traces VQA's development from Antol et al.'s benchmark dataset through visual language models to GPT-4V, and positions VQA as the cornerstone of multimodal AI for education.
requirements: A visual language model combining a computer vision model with a pre-trained LLM to bridge visual and textual modalities
constraints: Early VQA models had limited capability of understanding and generating long and sophisticated natural language inputs and outputs
target_learning_goals: analysis of image data from teaching and learning situations
examples: The article demonstrates VQA with GPT-4V on five educational image-analysis tasks using operating prompts
key_sources: Gyeong-Geon Lee and Xiaoming Zhai. (2024). Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07163

article_title: Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI
citation: Gyeong-Geon Lee and Xiaoming Zhai. (2024). Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07163
title: Use VQA as a draft judgment aid while the human instructor makes final instructional decisions
description: The article recommends that practitioners use VQA with simple prompts to draft their judgment on the current status of individual learners, small groups, and the classroom as a whole, while retaining human responsibility. It states that "the final assessment should be done by the human instructor, who could take responsibility to the instructional decisions." Used this way, the authors argue, VQA could dramatically reduce the time teachers need to deal with multimodal data and allow more intervention time.
requirements: Accessible VLM service usable through a chat interface without programming, such as GPT-4V on the ChatGPT chatbox with a GPT-4 subscription
constraints: GPT-4V sometimes provides scientifically or medically inappropriate information, which requires prudent use of it in terms of fact-checking
target_learners: school and university learners assessed by instructors using VQA
target_learning_goals: formative judgment about learners, groups, and classroom status; scoring constructed-response work
examples: The article's five demonstration tasks show GPT-4V drafting analyses of images, with scoring accuracy of 60% (structure) and 80% (distribution) against human coders
key_sources: Gyeong-Geon Lee and Xiaoming Zhai. (2024). Realizing Visual Question Answering for Education: GPT-4V as a Multimodal AI. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07163
